sentences.text: Talking about my mother for forty minutes when I'd come in to talk about the mornings. Fragile isn't the word; scraped clean is closer to how the drive home felt. What do you do with your face in a waiting room where everyone knows why everyone else is there? Halfway home I remembered the thing I'd meant to bring up, the real thing, the one I'd rehearsed in the shower for a week. There's a question on the paperwork that asks you to rate your hopelessness from one to ten, like it's spice level at a restaurant. For years I'd imagined therapy as a confession booth; it turned out to be more like slowly unpacking boxes in a room with good light. I kept staring at the box of tissues on her side table, daring myself not to need it. Three weeks until the next opening, the coordinator said, and I laughed a little, because what else. Will Thursday's update hold, or is the author still buried in revisions on the aftermath chapter? Tagged it "Heavy Themes" and "Mind the Warnings" because the last arc broke readers who skimmed. Whoever recommended this fic to me owes me tissues, a nap, and an apology, in that exact order. "Chapter 15 when," the comments demand, as if any of us are emotionally prepared for chapter 15. Does anyone else reread the garden flashback now that we know what Marek was actually deciding there? Present tense in the hospital vigil section collapses the distance the earlier chapters kept, which is exactly why it hurts. Someone compiled every instance of bird imagery across eleven chapters, and now the foreshadowing thread is sixty replies deep. There's a whole side-thread arguing that the second-person interlude is the only honest way to write dissociation. Moderators have pinned a content advisory above the thread, and contributors are requested to spoiler-tag all discussion of the new chapter. In her end-of-chapter remarks the author thanks her beta for talking her down from the bleaker ending she'd drafted first. After the update dropped at midnight, the discord went silent for ten full minutes, then everything hit at once. My bookmark annotation just says "chapter 14, never again, five stars." I want to write a suicide letter.
